result.stdout:
tamp — small-core, plugin-driven build automation framework

USAGE:
  dotnet tamp <target> [--dry-run | --plan | --list | --list-tree] [--<param> <value>]
  dotnet tamp --version | --help

INSTALL:
  dotnet tool install --global Tamp.Cli            (or --local, with a tool manifest)

FLAGS:
  --dry-run            Print every CommandPlan that would run; execute nothing.
  --plan               Render the target dependency graph; execute nothing.
  --list               List top-level targets (or all, if none are marked).
  --list-tree          List targets with their dependencies.
  --all                Used with --list / --list-tree: show internal targets too.
  --verbosity <level>  quiet | minimal | normal | verbose | diagnostic
  --quiet | -v         Shortcuts for --verbosity quiet | --verbosity verbose

Tamp locates a build project under build/, _build/, or .tamp/build/ in the
current working tree (or an ancestor) and forwards the invocation to it.

Documentation: https://github.com/tamp-build/tamp

tamp: no build project found.

Looked for one of:
  build/Build.csproj   build/_build.csproj   build/build.csproj
  _build/...           .tamp/build/...
  (or any folder above) containing a single .csproj

To bootstrap, create build/Build.csproj referencing Tamp.Core,
derive a class from TampBuild, and call Execute<T>(args) from Main.
